$comment: Vendor as .github/ci-evidence.json, with scripts/dev/release_evidence.py (docs/ci-evidence.md).
Every member below is required unless its comment says optional; an unknown member is refused.
"$comment" is allowed in any object whose members are fixed names, and is ignored.
Optional; absent is {"prerelease": false}: the release tag is vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, no leading zeroes.
true also admits a SemVer prerelease, vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-<identifier>(.<identifier>)*: identifiers of ASCII
letters, digits and hyphens, none empty, a numeric one without leading zeroes. Build metadata (+...) never.
Either way the tag must be annotated and name the exact release commit.
Optional; absent is {"validates": "none"}: a workflow_dispatch run of the release workflow does not use
the gate and is refused (dispatch-not-gated). "branch-tip": a dispatch on the trusted branch validates the
commit it ran for, the branch's tip, reads no tag, and decides "validated", never "reuse": no
publishing job may take it. Every other run of the release workflow is a publication, held to its tag.
Optional; absent is {"allowed": false}: evidence whose runner image or tools differ from what the
release runner resolves refuses (runtime-identity). true: a publication refused for that alone, under a
release-runner profile and after every other check passed, decides "revalidate": that evidence is not
taken, and the release workflow must run the check list dev.json declares on its own runner, strictly
(check.sh --setup --strict, then --all --strict), and publish only on that run's success. Work a CI job
does outside the check list is not re-run: run it in the release workflow (fresh_at_release) or keep this
false. A pin that does not match, a dispatch validation run and every other refusal still refuse.
compare release-runner: the release job, on the same platform, resolves the image and the tools itself;
a CI image or tool that differs from what it resolves refuses. The release job must run on this platform.
compare pins: for a leg the release job cannot resolve itself (another OS or architecture).
Every tool needs a pin, the exact text its command prints; ImageOS is optional and pins the image family.
path and name: the workflow file and its name: line. events: push, and workflow_dispatch if the fresh
route dispatches it; a dispatch that checks out another commit (an input sha) is refused by capture.
A run of another trigger on the branch at the commit (schedule, workflow_run, repository_dispatch) is
never evidence, but refuses reuse while unfinished or when newer than the selected run and not successful;
pull request and merge queue runs, other branches' and forks' runs neither count nor block.
skipped_jobs (optional): jobs that must have been skipped on the trusted branch, such as a pull-request-only job.
ci.name: CI

$comment: name: the job's display name as the API reports it; job_id: its key under jobs: in the workflow.
checks: the dev.json checks this job runs, or "all"; optional_skips (optional): checks it may skip;
setup (optional): true when the job's setup log is recorded too. A tag-sensitive check is never listed
here: the release workflow runs it itself, and fresh_at_release names it in the decision record.
check.name: check

$comment: A matrix leg is one entry: its display name with the matrix values, its own job key (the capture
step's --job, for example go-${{ matrix.os }}), and the job_id every leg shares.
go-macos.name: go (macos-latest)
